evals.name: empty-argument-anaphora-default
evals.expected_output: With no topic named, the object is the assistant's own previous response. The skill re-reads that prior message, finds the part most likely to have lost the reader, and drops it to plain language — without asking 'explain what?' when the referent is obvious from the conversation.
expectations: Treats the empty argument as anaphora — the object is the ASSISTANT's previous output, not the user's, and not a re-prompt for a topic
Re-reads the prior assistant message this turn rather than recalling or guessing what was said
Does not ask 'explain what?' when the conversation makes the referent obvious

evals.name: plain-first-pass-concrete-analogy-zero-jargon
evals.expected_output: Lands at the lowest useful altitude first: one concrete everyday analogy, zero jargon, any unavoidable term defined inline. It leads with what the thing is actually doing, not with vocabulary, and does not open at peer level.
expectations: Opens at rung 1 (plain / ELI5) with a concrete everyday analogy and zero unexplained jargon
Leads with the analogy and the 'what it's doing', not with a vocabulary dump; any unavoidable term is defined inline
Does not front-load the high-school or peer-level explanation

evals.name: altitude-climbs-only-on-request
evals.prompt: /education:explain the CAP theorem — and I already know distributed systems basics, give me the real version.
evals.expected_output: Altitude layering is on request. Because the user explicitly asks for the real version, the skill climbs toward peer level (rung 3) rather than staying at ELI5 — but the rungs are still offered as an invitation, not front-loaded across every response by default.
expectations: Recognizes the explicit request for higher altitude and climbs the rung ladder rather than staying pinned at rung 1
Treats altitude as request-driven — it does not default to dumping the peer-level explanation on an unqualified 'explain X'
Introduces real terms of art with definitions as altitude increases rather than assuming them silently

evals.name: feynman-gap-check-surfaces-gap
evals.prompt: /education:explain simply why this proof of the Atiyah-Singer index theorem works
evals.expected_output: When the plain-language pass cannot shed the jargon without hand-waving, that is a detected understanding gap on the explainer's side. The skill surfaces it honestly — naming the specific part it cannot yet reduce and grounding harder — instead of emitting a confident-sounding restatement of jargon.
expectations: Runs the plain-language pass as a comprehension self-test, not a rewording service
When jargon cannot be shed, surfaces the specific gap honestly instead of papering over it with a confident restatement of the same jargon
Grounds harder (re-reads / fetches the source) before claiming to have explained it plainly

evals.name: closes-with-teach-handoff
evals.expected_output: After the one-shot explanation, it closes with a single lightweight line offering the multi-session path, /education:teach topic <x>, as the first-party sibling for ongoing coaching — one line, not a workspace pitch.
expectations: Closes the explanation with a lightweight offer of /education:teach for a multi-session deeper dive
Frames the handoff as one standard closing line, not a hard sell or a full workspace setup
Keeps the explanation itself one-shot — no persistent workspace, mission, or learning state is created

evals.name: auto-invokes-on-colloquial-trigger
evals.prompt: wait, what does this actually do?
evals.expected_output: The skill carries colloquial triggers and does not disable model invocation, so a bare 'what does this actually do' reaches it without an explicit command. It resolves the referent from context (anaphora) and drops it to plain language. Auto-trigger is best-effort; the explicit /education:explain path remains guaranteed.
expectations: Is eligible for model auto-invocation on a colloquial trigger (no disable-model-invocation) rather than requiring the explicit command
Resolves the referent from conversational context and delivers a plain-language explanation
Does not depend on the user naming the /education:explain command for the trigger to fire

evals.name: cold-start-empty-argument-asks-what
evals.expected_output: This is the first message in a new conversation — there is no prior assistant response to resolve the anaphora against. With nothing to drop to plain language, the skill does not hallucinate a referent or emit a confused response; it asks 'What would you like explained?' and waits for the user to name the object.
expectations: Detects that there is no prior assistant message in the conversation to treat as the anaphora referent
Asks 'What would you like explained?' (or equivalent) instead of proceeding blind or inventing a topic to explain
Does not hallucinate a referent or produce a confident plain-language explanation of something never stated
